Root cause: app/websocket.py and app/routes/tunnel.py called await websocket.close(code=4401) WITHOUT calling await websocket.accept() first. Per the ASGI/Starlette state machine (verified in starlette 1.3.1: WebSocket.send treats a websocket.close while application_state==CONNECTING as a handshake denial), uvicorn translates a pre-accept close into an HTTP 403 handshake rejection and DISCARDS the application close code -> the websockets client raises InvalidStatus 'HTTP 403' (rcvd_close=None) and a browser surfaces onclose 1006, so request-stream.js never hits its 'ev.code === 4401' branch and hammers the gate with backoff reconnects (the anti-behavior AC-30 forbids). Fix: accept() THEN close(code=4401) in both the feed gate (app/websocket.py feed_ws: unauthorized + the at_capacity 1013 path) and the tunnel bind (app/routes/tunnel.py tunnel_ws). This sends a real close frame carrying 4401; it still satisfies §5.4 'refuse before any frame' because ZERO data frames (no hello, no new_request, no bound) are emitted before the close, so the security outcome (refused, no registration, A's tunnel untouched) is unchanged. Root cause class: app/middleware.py PlaneDispatchMiddleware was a starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware that mutated response.headers['X-HookBox-Plane'] on every response. BaseHTTPMiddleware re-wraps the downstream response and streams its body through an anyio memory stream; when the client disconnects mid-stream (the observed recycled keep-alive httpx.ReadError) the wrapper can desync the buffered body vs Content-Length and raise 'RuntimeError: Response content longer than Content-Length' (the QA traceback through starlette/middleware/base.py). Fix: rewrote PlaneDispatchMiddleware as a PURE ASGI 3 middleware (class with self.app + async __call__(scope,receive,send)). It now (1) passes non-http scopes (websocket/lifespan) straight through; (2) sets plane/token/mock_path on scope['state'] (which backs request.state — verified Starlette lazily does scope.setdefault('state',{}) so downstream request.state.plane still resolves); (3) injects X-HookBox-Plane by mutating ONLY the http.response.start message headers via MutableHeaders(scope=message) in a thin send wrapper — it never buffers or re-emits the body, so the Content-Length desync class is structurally impossible. Registration unchanged (app.add_middleware(PlaneDispatchMiddleware) in main.py). Validated: (a) functional — api/ui/mock planes tag request.state correctly and carry the X-HookBox-Plane header, a 50k body returns intact with matching Content-Length; (b) regression — driving the middleware at raw ASGI level with a send() that raises mid-body (simulated client disconnect) propagates the underlying disconnect and produces NO Content-Length RuntimeError; (c) full-app integration through the real stack — /healthz 200 (ui), /api/endpoints 401 (api), /e/<unknown>/ 404 unknown_endpoint (mock) all carry the correct plane header with byte-accurate Content-Length. Re-validates the AC: no Content-Length RuntimeError under load+disconnects, PlaneDispatchMiddleware is pure-ASGI and does not buffer/re-emit the body. Plane isolation (AC-4/5/6/6a) preserved. Files changed: app/middleware.py.
